newsitem.title: BRAZIL: New Brazil tax scares blns in foreign money - paper.
newsitem.headline: New Brazil tax scares blns in foreign money - paper.

text.p: Foreign investors, wary of Brazil's new CPMF check tax, are pulling money out of the country via the forex floating rate market at a rate of $60 million a day, Gazeta Mercantil financial daily said.
Gazeta, citing preliminary Central Bank figures, said the outflow is expected to reach $1.3 billion in December and $12 billion for the year.
The 0.2-percent CPMF tax on all financial transactions is expected to be levied starting January 23.
"I think the volume of speculative foreign capital that can leave the country is running out," the paper quoted Central Bank Foreign Affairs Director Gustavo Franco as saying.

But the entrance of direct foreign investment and external loans is enough to offset the outflow of speculative capital, cover the trade deficit and guarantee a $10 billion surplus on the balance of payments, he said.
Senior government officials, saying the CPMF will hurt Brazilian financial markets by reducing volume, said Brasilia is studying whether to exempt stock transactions from the tax.
